Rewrite the passage for Grade 0 readers:

Maria is learning to add numbers. She enjoys adding numbers because it is fun! She can add one and one to make two, and she knows that two and two make four. She also knows that three and three make six. But she didn't know what happens when you add four and four. So she asked her mom. Her mom said that four and four make eight. Maria was happy because now she knows! She is four years old now, and in four more years, she will be eight. Maria is a clever learner. She learns quickly.

Rewrite the passage for Grade 2 readers:

Maria was learning to add numbers. She enjoyed adding numbers because it was fun! She could easily add one and one together to make two. And two plus two made four. Three plus three also made six. But she wondered, what is four plus four? So she asked her mom. Her mom told her that four plus four equals eight. Maria smiled and said, "Now I know!" Because this year, she turned 4. In four more years, she will turn 8! Maria was a quick learner. She wasn't a slow learner.

Rewrite the passage so it is appropriate for Grade 4 readers:
Maria learned to add numbers. She enjoyed adding numbers because it was simple and fun. She knew how to add one and one, which equals two. And she knew that two and two make four. But when it came to three and three, she realized there was a problem - the answer should be six, not nine! So she didn't know what four and four would equal. After thinking for a while, Maria asked her mom. Her mom explained that four and four equals eight. "Oh, I see!" Maria said. "Since I am already four years old, in four more years I will turn eight." Maria was clever and quick to learn new things.

Rewrite the passage so it is suitable for Grade 6 readers:

Maria enjoyed practicing her addition skills. She found adding numbers to be simple and fun. She easily remembered that one plus one equals two, and two plus two equals four. She also knew that three added to itself results in six. However, she struggled with finding the sum of four and four. Seeking help from her mom, Maria discovered that the answer was indeed eight. "Ah, I've got it now," she said enthusiastically. "In four years, I will be turning eight." Demonstrating quick learning abilities, Maria was certainly on the path to mastering math.

Rewrite the passage so that it is appropriate for Grade 8 readers:

Maria was practicing addition. She enjoyed working with numbers and finding their sums. However, she found herself stumped when trying to add larger numbers together. Specifically, she didn't know the value of four plus four. Intrigued, she asked her mother for help. Her mom explained that four plus four equals eight. Maria was delighted with this newfound knowledge and made a connection between her age and this mathematical fact: in four more years, she would turn eight herself. Maria demonstrated a quick understanding of mathematics and a keen ability to learn. She was not struggling with the concepts presented.

Rewrite the passage for Grade 10 readers:

Maria, a young mathematician in the making, was delving into the realm of arithmetic, specifically addition. Her enthusiasm for numbers was palpable, finding solace in the simplicity and logic they presented. Adding numbers, to Maria, was second nature - she could effortlessly combine ones, twos, and threes with ease. However, her understanding stalled when it came to four-digit numbers. Puzzled, she approached her mother for assistance. Her mother explained that when four is added to four, the sum equals eight. "Ah, now I understand," Maria exclaimed. "At present, I am four years old. In another four years, I will turn eight." Maria's intellectual prowess was evident, as she swiftly grasped mathematical concepts that left many her age behind.

Rewrite the passage for Grade 12 readers:

Maria was developing her understanding of basic arithmetic operations. She found numerical addition particularly engaging. The process of adding numbers proved to be an easy and straightforward endeavor for Maria, as she could effortlessly combine any two single-digit numbers. For example, one plus one equals two, two plus two equals four, three plus three equals six. However, this was where her knowledge plateaued; she was uncertain about the result of adding together four and four. Intrigued, Maria sought guidance from her mother, who confirmed that four plus four indeed equates to eight. Filled with newfound understanding, Maria remarked, "Now I comprehend." Acknowledging her own age, she mused that in another four years, she would reach the same numeric age of eight. Maria demonstrated a remarkable aptitude for learning mathematical concepts at a rapid pace, indicating an advanced level of intellectual curiosity and potential.

Rewrite the following passage for Grade 0 readers:

It was a special day! It was New Year's Day. A boy named [Hero] lived in a city called Las Vegas. He got into his car and went to a fun place called a casino. He walked to a game called roulette. He bought one chip with $100 money. He flipped a coin. He caught the coin. It was heads! The boy put the chip on a red spot on the roulette table. The dealer spun the wheel. The wheel went round and round. The dealer pushed a silver ball. The ball went round and round. The wheel stopped moving. The ball stopped too. The ball landed in a red spot. The boy won $100! The dealer gave him another chip with $100 money. The boy thanked the dealer by giving him a $10 gift. The boy took both his chips to get more money. He went home and felt very happy. He thought this year would be a great year for him.

Rewrite the passage for Grade 2 readers:

It was New Year's Day! A boy named [Name] lived in a city called Las Vegas. He drove a car to a place called a casino. At the casino, he walked to a game called roulette. There, he bought one chip for $100 dollars. He flipped a coin and caught it. It was heads! So, he placed his chip on the red part of the roulette table.

The dealer (a person who works at the casino) turned the roulette wheel. The wheel spun around and around. The dealer pushed a small silver ball. The ball also started spinning. Then, the wheel slowed down. The ball slowed down too. Finally, the ball landed in a red slot! He won!

The dealer gave him another $100 chip. The boy then gave the dealer $10 as a thank-you gift. He traded both his chips for money. He went home and felt happy because he thought it would be a great year.

Rewrite this passage for Grade 4 readers:

A boy celebrated New Year's Day in Las Vegas. He drove to a casino and walked to a roulette table. He bought one chip worth $100. He tossed a coin, caught it, and it landed on heads. He bet the chip on red. The dealer spun the wheel. Round and round went the wheel. The dealer pushed a silver ball around the edge of the wheel. Slower and slower went the wheel and the ball. Finally, the ball dropped into a slot that was red! The boy won! The dealer gave him another $100 chip. The boy thanked the dealer with a $10 tip. He cashed in both his chips. Then, he went home feeling happy. He thought it was going to be a great year ahead.

Rewrite the passage so that it is appropriate for Grade 6 readers:

It was New Year's Day. A person lived in Las Vegas. They drove to a casino. They walked to a roulette table. They bought one chip for $100. They flipped a coin. They caught the coin. It landed on tails, but they decided to bet anyway. They put the $100 chip on red. The dealer spun the roulette wheel. The wheel started spinning quickly. The dealer pushed a small silver ball. The ball bounced around the wheel. The wheel slowed down. The ball stopped in a red slot. They won! The dealer gave them another $100 chip. They gave the dealer a $5 tip. They cashed in both their chips. They went home. They felt happy and excited. They thought it was going to be a great year.

Rewrite the passage so it is suitable for 8th-grade readers:

It was New Year's Day. He lived in Las Vegas. He drove to a casino. He walked to a roulette table. He bought one chip worth $100. He flipped a coin. He caught the coin. It landed on heads. Excited, he put his $100 chip on a red number on the table. The dealer spun the wheel. The wheel started spinning quickly. The dealer pushed a silver ball. The ball began to spin too. The wheel started slowing down. So did the ball. Finally, the ball landed in a slot with a red number - he had won! The dealer gave him another $100 chip. He then gave the dealer a $10 tip as a thank you. He cashed in both his chips. With a smile on his face, he went home feeling happy. He knew it was going to be a good year.

Rewrite the passage for Grade 10 readers, using simpler language and clearer sentence structure:

On New Year's Day, he lived in Las Vegas. He drove to a casino. He walked up to a roulette table. He bought one chip worth $100. He flipped a coin. He caught the coin. It was heads. He placed the $100 chip on red. The dealer spun the wheel. The wheel spun around and around. The dealer rolled the silver ball. The ball also spun around and around. The wheel and ball started to slow down. The ball dropped into a slot that was red. He won! The dealer gave him another $100 chip. He gave the dealer a $10 tip. He cashed in both his chips. He went home. He felt happy. It seemed like it would be a great year.

Rewrite the following passage for Grade 12 readers:

On January 1st, an individual residing in Las Vegas decided to visit a casino. Upon arrival, he navigated towards a roulette table and purchased a single chip worth $100. After flipping the coin, he successfully caught it mid-air, which revealed heads. With this result, he placed his $100 chip on the red section of the roulette table.

As the dealer spun the wheel, the cacophony of the casino surrounded him as the silver ball embarked on its own whirlwind journey around the table. The momentum gradually lessened, and anticipation built as both the wheel and ball slowed down. Finally, the ball landed in a red slot, resulting in a win for our protagonist.

The dealer returned his $100 chip and he generously tipped the dealer $10. Having cashed out both of his chips, he left the casino feeling victorious and optimistic about the year ahead.

Rewrite the following text for Grade 0 readers:

Soccer is a fun game that lots of people like to play. It's popular everywhere in the world! People watch and play soccer because it's exciting. There are two teams, each with players who kick a big ball across a big green field. The goal is to get the ball into the other team's net at the end of the field. The players can use their feet, chests, or heads to move the ball, but they must not touch it with their hands. Players run around, sometimes sliding on the grass and bumping into each other. They try hard to win!

Rewrite the following passage for Grade 2 readers:

Soccer is a fun game that lots of people enjoy! It's popular everywhere. People like to watch it, and they like to play it too. Soccer is easy to understand because there are only two teams playing on a big field with grass. The teams try to get a ball into the other team's goal, which has a net in front of it. Players can't use their hands to move the ball; they must use their feet, chests, or heads instead! Sometimes players run fast back and forth, slide on the grass, bump into each other, but all this is part of trying to win the game.

Rewrite the following passage for 4th grade readers:

Soccer is a great game that lots of people enjoy. It's played in many countries, and it can be lots of fun to watch or play! The field where they play soccer is big and grassy, with two teams competing against each other. Each team has one ball to try to get into the other team's goal. They can't use their hands; instead, they use their feet, chests, or heads to move the ball. The players run back and forth, slide on the grass, and sometimes bump into each other while playing to win!

Rewrite the following passage for 6th grade readers:

Soccer is an exciting game that's enjoyed by many people around the world. It's fun to watch, and it's even more thrilling to play! The game takes place on a large green field with two teams. Each team tries to score points by kicking the ball into the other team's goal using only their feet, chests, or heads. There are no hands allowed, and the players run back and forth trying to avoid colliding with each other while strategizing to win the game. Sometimes, they slide on the grass for extra speed!

Rewrite the passage for 8th-grade readers:

Soccer is an enjoyable sport that's widely appreciated across the globe. It's exciting to watch and even more fun to participate in! Here's a brief overview of the game. Two teams face off on a large, green field. One ball is used, and there are two goals equipped with nets. The aim of each team is to score by kicking the ball into the opposing team's goal without using their hands. Players use various body parts to maneuver the ball, such as their feet, chests, and heads. During play, you'll often see them dashing back and forth, sliding on the grass, colliding with each other, and tirelessly competing for victory!

Rewrite the passage so that it is appropriate for Grade 10 readers:

Soccer, also known as football, is a widely enjoyed sport with a global following. It's not only exciting to spectate but also a thrill to participate in. The basic rules and concept of the game are straightforward. Two teams compete on a large, grassy field, each aiming to score points by maneuvering a single ball into the opposing team's net using any part of their body except their hands. Commonly, players employ their feet, chests, or heads to control and advance the ball. The game involves continuous running, sliding on the grass, and occasional collisions between players as they strive for victory.

Rewrite the passage for a Grade 12 audience, maintaining the informal tone but using more complex vocabulary and sentence structure:

Soccer, an engaging sport, enjoys widespread appeal across global communities. Its entertainment value is multifaceted; both as a spectator's delight and an appealing pastime for participants. The game, although seemingly straightforward in its essence, possesses intricate strategies that unfold dynamically on the expansive green canvas of a field.

Two competing teams confront each other on this verdant expanse, armed with only one spherical object: the ball. Their objective is to maneuver the ball into the opposing team's goal, protected by a net. However, unlike most games where hands are the primary tool for manipulation, soccer enforces stringent rules prohibiting any direct contact between players and the ball with their hands.

Instead, soccer players employ a variety of body parts to manipulate the ball - legs for propulsion, chests for precise control, heads for powerful strikes, and feet for deft flicks. The game is characterized by the relentless movement of players; they dart back and forth, perform sliding tackles on the grass, collide with each other, all in an attempt to outwit their opponents. Ultimately, the objective remains clear: to secure a victory.

Rewrite the passage for Grade 0 readers:

Dad and his boy named Chris went to watch a baseball game together. The team called the Dodgers was playing against the Giants. The Dodgers stayed at home, while the Giants came from far away. Dad and Chris walked into a big stadium called Dodger Stadium. Many people were there, and most of them wanted the Dodgers to win and the Giants to lose. After finding their seats, Dad and Chris sat down. The game had already begun. Chris said he was hungry. So, his dad bought two bags of yummy peanuts for him. He also got two hot dogs and a big drink for Chris. A ball that wasn't caught came towards them, and people tried to get it. They accidentally knocked over Chris' drink. But, his dad quickly bought him another drink.

Rewrite the following passage so it is appropriate for 2nd grade readers: Dad took his son Chris to see the baseball game. The Dodgers were playing against the Giants at Dodger Stadium, where the Dodgers were the team at home and the Giants were visitors. Many people went to watch the game, most of them hoping that the Dodgers would win while the Giants lost. Dad and Chris found their seats in the stadium, sat down, and watched as the game had already started. Chris told his dad he was hungry, so Dad bought him two bags of peanuts, two hot dogs, and a big soda. Suddenly, a ball went flying towards them! People quickly tried to catch it, but they accidentally knocked over Chris's soda. His dad bought him another one right away.

Rewrite the following passage for Grade 4 readers:

Dad took his son, named Chris, to watch a baseball match. The team called the Los Angeles Dodgers was playing against the San Francisco Giants. The Dodgers were the ones playing at home, while the Giants were there to play as visitors. Dad and Chris walked into Dodger Stadium, where lots of people had gathered. Most of them hoped that the Dodgers would win, and the Giants would lose. After finding their seats, they sat down just as the game was about to start. Suddenly, Chris told his dad he was feeling hungry. So, Dad bought two bags of peanuts, two hot dogs, and a big soda for Chris. However, when a ball went off course towards them, people tried to catch it. In the process, they accidentally knocked over Chris' soda. Dad then purchased another soda for Chris.

Rewrite the passage so that it is appropriate for Grade 8 readers: Dad took his son, Chris, to a baseball game. The Los Angeles Dodgers were playing against the San Francisco Giants at Dodger Stadium. The Dodgers were the home team, and the Giants were the visiting team. Dad and Chris walked into the crowded stadium. Most of the people there were rooting for the Dodgers to win and for the Giants to lose. Rewrite the following passage for 10th-grade readers:

During a baseball game, Dad took his son named Chris to see the Los Angeles Dodgers compete against the San Francisco Giants at Dodger Stadium. The Dodgers were the hosts, while the Giants were visiting. A large crowd had gathered, with most spectators hoping for a Dodgers victory and a loss for the Giants. When Dad and Chris arrived, they located their seats and settled in as the game was already underway. Chris mentioned to his father that he felt hungry, prompting Dad to purchase two bags of peanuts and two hot dogs for Chris. Additionally, Dad bought a large soda for Chris. However, a stray ball came flying in their direction, causing spectators to dive for it. Unfortunately, the commotion resulted in Chris's soda being spilled. Dad quickly bought him another drink to replace it.

New passage (for 10th-grade readers):

Dad accompanied his son Chris to a baseball game featuring the Los Angeles Dodgers and San Francisco Giants at Dodger Stadium. As the hometown team, the Dodgers were anticipating victory, while the Giants' opponents hoped for their defeat. Upon entering, Dad and Chris joined the crowd of spectators. They soon found their seats and sat down as the game had already begun. Chris expressed his hunger to his father, leading Dad to buy two bags of peanuts, two hot dogs, and a large soda for his son. A foul ball then came close, causing people to dive for it, which unfortunately toppled Chris's drink. His father quickly purchased him another beverage to replace the spilled one.

Rewrite the following passage suitable for Grade 12 readers:

During an evening, the father accompanied his adult son, Christopher, to a Major League Baseball game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the San Francisco Giants at Dodger Stadium. The Dodgers were hosting the series as their home team, while the Giants represented the visiting team. The atmosphere inside the stadium was electric, with most spectators rooting for the Dodgers' victory and the defeat of the Giants. Upon entering their seats, Christopher expressed hunger to his father. In response, his father purchased two bags of salted peanuts, two hot dogs, and a large fountain drink for his son. As the game progressed, a foul ball unexpectedly headed towards them. Amidst the chaotic attempts by several individuals to secure the ball, it knocked over Christopher's drink. His father swiftly bought him another beverage to replace it.

Friend: Ugh, I'm really stressed out. The library doesn't seem to have any books related to my research topic.
Suggestion: Have you checked other libraries? You might find what you're looking for there.
Response: Not really, I don't want to spend gas money driving around.
Counter-suggestion: Well, it might be worth it since you could potentially save time by finding the book faster. Any suggestions on which library to try?
Recommendation: There's a library near my house that has a vast collection. It's never failed me before.
Objection: That sounds like it's too far for me to travel.
Alternative Proposal: I have an idea – what if I borrow the books from that library and bring them to you?
Concern: I'm not sure about that, what if something happens to the books while they're in my possession?
Promise: Don't worry, I promise I'll take good care of them. I'd never intentionally lose or damage someone else's property.
Impression: That's very responsible of you. Alright, let me give it some thought and we can discuss further later on.

Rewrite the conversation to suit a more formal, Grade 12 reading level:

The individual expressed frustration due to the inability to locate any relevant literature for their research topic within their personal library. They inquired if another library may yield more promising results. However, there was apprehension regarding potential fuel costs associated with visiting a different library. A suggestion was made for an alternative library nearby the advisor's residence. The individual objected to this due to the distance being unfeasible. The advisor insisted on this particular library's extensive collection and reliability in providing suitable literature. A proposal ensued, suggesting that the individual could borrow the required books from the advisor. This was met with concern over potential book loss, to which the individual assured that they would take every precaution to avoid such an eventuality. The conversation concluded with the individual's acknowledgement of the advisor's seriousness and commitment in securing the necessary resources for their research.

Hello Friend Samia,

I am writing to tell you something fun! How about meeting on Saturday instead of Sunday? That works for me because I have plans with my family on Sunday. If that's okay for you, would you like to visit our new home? You can see our nice flat and the kitchen we made better since we moved in. We will eat at home and then go for a walk together in the afternoon. It will be so much fun to catch up! I want to hear all about your new job.

Our house is on 52 Charles Road, but it might be hard to find because the house numbers are strange here. After you pass the post office, turn left and keep going past the big white house on Charles Road. Behind it, there's a small street with houses numbered 50-56. I don't understand why this little street doesn't have its own name! If you get lost, just call me, and I will come to help you.

Let me know if there are any foods you like or dislike so we can make sure to have something you enjoy. I am very excited to see you soon!

See you later, friend!

Gregor
